newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian lawmakers trapped by Israeli closure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian lawmakers trapped by Israeli closure.

text.p: Palestinian lawmakers from Gaza attending a parliamentary session in Ramallah were trapped on Thursday by Israel's closure of the West Bank town after Arab gunmen killed two Jewish settlers nearby, a lawmaker said.

Sheikh Wajeeh Yaghi said Israeli soldiers were preventing about 20 legislators from leaving Ramallah for Gaza, holding them at a checkpoint which the Israelis set up at the western entrance to the city.
"This is shameful. We have been sitting here in cold weather for more than one hour. We have shown the Israelis our VIP passes, but they are refusing to honour them," Yaghi told Reuters by phone.
An Israeli army spokesman said he was checking the report.
Israel on Wednesday encircled the PLO-ruled twin towns of Ramallah and al-Bireh, home to more than 60,000 Palestinians, with military roadblocks preventing anyone from leaving or entering.
The closure was intended to pressure the Palestinian Authority to search for and apprehend the killers of the two settlers, whom Israel said fled to Ramallah.

Israel regulates travel between the West Bank and Gaza Strip with permits issued by its military authorities. High-ranking Palestinian officials receive VIP permits allowing them more freedom of movement.
